The lexer now accepts the C23 `_BitInt` literal suffixes `wb` and `WB`, alone or combined with `u`/`U` in either order (`12wb`, `12uWB`, `0x1fUWB`). Mixed case like `wB` is not accepted. `pytest tests -q` passes with 247 passed and 6 skipped. I also ran the declared owned check, which reported "incomplete" even though the child exit code was 0, so I can't say it passed.

The change is in `_integer_suffix_opt` in `pycparser/c_lexer.py`, and it applies to decimal, octal, hex and binary constants. I added four lexer assertions to `tests/test_c_lexer.py` covering decimal and hex forms.

I didn't touch the parser or generator. The suffix stays in the token text, so existing handling of integer constants should pass it through unchanged. I did not test parsing or regenerating C code that uses these literals.
